headline_footnote: Revenue grew 36% on 16% more volume — driven mainly by breadth: 20 more active cafés and double the new-account intake.
derived_footnote: * Assumption: new accounts are counted within active cafés and each placed ~1 order. June's 56 active exceeds May's 36 + 14 new (50) — at least 6 dormant accounts likely reactivated.
performance_statement: June's headline is strong: revenue grew 36% to £21,042 on 150.5kg, 73 orders and 56 active cafés, with 14 new accounts onboarded — double May's intake. But the growth was led by breadth, not depth: the active base grew 56% while revenue grew 36%, so revenue per café fell 13% and orders per café fell 22%. At the same time, realised price per kg rose 17% and AOV rose 12% — when cafés order, they order higher-value. The open question: is the drop in order frequency healthy dilution from a big onboarding month, or early softening in the existing base? We can't yet tell without account-level order tracking — paired with the continued absence of margin data, that's the gap to close before July.
net_summary: a strong, encouraging month with genuine positives — revenue, pricing power, and a widening returning base — alongside one metric to watch closely: per-account order frequency.

insights.title: Strong, breadth-led month
insights.body: Revenue rose 36% to £21,042, but the active base grew faster (+56%). More cafés buying, not each café buying more.

insights.title: Pricing power showed up (+17%/kg)
insights.body: Revenue grew more than twice as fast as volume — the gap is price/mix. Confirm the cause before banking on it.

insights.title: Order frequency softened (−22%)
insights.body: Partly dilution from doubling onboards, but the returning base still appears to have slowed. Timing or real softening — can't yet tell.

insights.title: The base is widening
insights.body: Returning/reactivated accounts grew ~29 → ~42 (+45%), partly offsetting the frequency dip.

insights.title: Two things still invisible
insights.body: No margin data (is £21k more profitable than May's £15.5k?) and no account-level order history. Closing these is the highest-value move for July.

recommendations_intro: Grounded in this month's numbers — not generic advice.

recommendations.title: Convert the sample backlog first
recommendations.body: 80 cafés currently sit at 'sample sent' vs 71 active — a bigger pool than the entire active base. A simple 2-3 week follow-up after each sample (call or WhatsApp) is likely the cheapest lever available for new-account growth right now.

recommendations.title: Protect reorder frequency
recommendations.body: Orders per active café fell 22% this month. A lightweight reorder reminder timed to each café's typical cycle (e.g. 3-4 weeks after last order) could arrest the slide before it becomes a trend.

recommendations.title: Close the margin gap before scaling further
recommendations.body: We can't yet confirm whether June's £21k is more profitable than May's £15.5k. Capture cost-per-kg and fulfilment cost next — it's the single highest-value data investment on the table.

recommendations.title: Lean into the pricing signal
recommendations.body: Realised price/kg rose 17% this month. Worth testing whether that holds for new accounts too, or introducing a premium SKU — early evidence suggests cafés will pay for quality.
